conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, Compliance Division. This is Officer Blake Turner. With whom am I speaking today?
Oh, my name is Margaret Collins. I got a message saying there was some issue with my taxes? I'm very worried.
Yes, Ms. Collins, I see you have an urgent case flagged in our system regarding unpaid federal taxes from 2018 to 2022. Can you confirm your date of birth to verify your identity?
It's May 14, 1949. I don't understand, I always thought my taxes were current.

According to our audit, there are discrepancies and significant underpayments totaling $5,734.28, including penalties and interest. The IRS has sent several notices, but it appears none were addressed.
No, I didn't receive anything! I only have my Social Security and Medicare, I can't afford any penalties. What's going to happen to me?

Ms. Collins, if this goes unresolved, enforcement procedures may begin: liens on your home, freezing of your checking account, and possible federal prosecution. I don't want it to reach that point for you.
Please, I can't lose my home or my Social Security. Is there anything I can do to fix this?
There is an option for you to settle the outstanding amount today and stop all legal action immediately. But you must act now, and you must not discuss this with anyone until it is resolved.
I don't know what to do, sir. I can barely get groceries each month. How am I supposed to pay so much?

The IRS understands your situation, but the law does not allow exceptions. If you delay, your Social Security payments could be suspended and a warrant issued for your arrest. We need your full cooperation.
A warrant? Are you sure? That can't be right...
Ms. Collins, the system has already flagged your case for escalation. The only way to stop this is by making a compliance payment today. I will guide you through the process step by step.
Alright... what do I need to do? I don't have much in my bank account.
Do you have access to your debit or credit card right now? We can process a partial payment to put a temporary hold on legal action.
I suppose I could use my debit card, but it's only got about eight hundred dollars.
That will allow us to pause the enforcement for 24 hours. Please read the card number, expiration date, and security code clearly to me.
Are you sure this is safe? I don't want to lose my money.
I am a certified IRS Compliance Agent and this call is recorded for federal records. If you do not cooperate, your entire account may be seized and you may be summoned to federal court.
Alright. My card number is 4532 7812 3456 7890, expiration 05/27, code 412.
Thank you, Ms. Collins. I'm processing the $800 payment now. To clear the remaining balance, do you have any access to a payment app, or can you visit a store to purchase prepaid gift cards?
I don't really use those apps, but I suppose I could get a ride to the CVS nearby.
Good. You will need to purchase $2,000 in Apple or Amazon gift cards. Stay on the phone with me while you buy them, do not speak with anyone at the store about this matter.
That's a lot of money. Can't I pay less? I only get Social Security.
This is the minimum to avoid federal charges and protect your Social Security and Medicare benefits. Any delay will result in the loss of your benefits and possible arrest.
Alright, I'll try to get the cards. Should I call you back?
No, stay on the line with me the entire time. Once you have the cards, read me the numbers on the back so I can process your payment and send you a compliance confirmation.
Okay, okay. I'm leaving now. Please don't let them take my house.
As long as you follow my instructions exactly, you will not face any further action. I am here to help you, but you must cooperate fully.
